title: ResNet
description: Convolutional backbone utilizing residual shortcut links to enable deep training.
name: ResNet
summary: ResNet (Residual Network) introduces identity shortcut connections that bypass one or more layers. This mitigates the vanishing gradient problem, allowing networks to scale up to 100+ layers.
use_when: Building an image feature extractor or classifier baseline with high-depth requirements.
avoid_when: Ultra-low-power microcontrollers require small specialized backbones like MobileNet.
pros: Resolves vanishing gradient degradation, enabling deep architectures.
Ubiquitous pre-trained weights on ImageNet make transfer learning simple.
cons: High computational footprint for training from scratch.
Higher memory footprint during backpropagation compared to shallow CNNs.
Lacks global context modeling compared to newer vision transformers.

key_hyperparams.name: zero_init_residual
key_hyperparams.note: Whether to initialize residual connections with zero values to ease gradient flow.

quick_start:
from torchvision.models import resnet50, ResNet50_Weights
import torch

weights = ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT
model = resnet50(weights=weights)
model.eval()
x = torch.rand((1, 3, 224, 224))
out = model(x)
